 JUDGMENT

This claim petition is filed by the petitioners under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1989 claiming compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- along with interest from the respondents on account of death of one Mahalingappa, who is the father of the petitioners No.1 and 2.
2.

Briefly stated the case of the petitioners is as follows:
That on 02.05.2019 at about 6.30 p.m., the deceased Mahalingappa was proceeding as a pillion rider on Honda Activa motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-04-HS-8642 along with his son Veeresh, being the rider of the motorcycle and when they reached near Defence Colony, 3 rd cross road, Bengaluru city, the rider of another motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-05-JX-9971 came with high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motorcycle in which deceased was a pillion rider.

Due to the impact deceased sustained grievous injuries and he took treatment in Arunodaya hospital, Bengaluru, Prakriya hospital and Sapthagiri hospital and on 16.05.2019, the deceased succumbed to the injuries .
A case was registered against the rider of the motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-05-JX-9971 in Crime No.78/2019 at Peenya Traffic Police Station.
Hence, this petition for compensation.
3. In response to the notice, the respondent No.2 has not chosen to appear before the Court and he was placed exparte.
The respondent No.1 has appeared before the Court through his Advocate, but he has failed to contest the petition by filing written statement.

4. On behalf of the petitioners, the petitioner No.2 is examined as PW-1, two witnesses are examined as PWs 2 and 3 and got marked Exs.P.1 to P.31.
5.
Heard the arguments.

6. On the basis of the above pleadings, following points arise for consideration:

sentences.text: Whether the Petitioners prove that the deceased succumbed to the injuries in a Motor Vehicle Accident that occurred on 02.05.2019 at about 6.30 p.m. near 3rd cross road, Defence Colony, Bengaluru, within the jurisdiction of Peenya Traffic Police station on account of rash and negligent riding of the motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-05-JX-9971 by its rider?

2. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation as prayed for ? If so at what rate and from whom?
3. What order or award?

7. My findings on the above points are as follows:
Point No.1 ...
In the Affirmative, Point No.2 ...
Partly in affirmative, compensation of Rs.6,75,000/- from the respondents Point No.3 ...

As per final order for the following:-
REASONS 8. Point No.1:- The petitioners in order to prove their case have placed reliance on the oral evidence of PW1 and documentary evidence as per Exhibits P.1 to P.11, P.26, P.27, P.29 and P.30 such as FIR,
complaint , spot sketch, spot panchanama , IMV report, P.M.Report, Inquest Panchanama, P.F.,
chargesheet, notice under Section 133 of M.V.Act, reply to notice, MLC register extracts and case sheets. PW-1 being the son of the deceased in his evidence has narrated how his father met with an accident and the accident was due to the rash and negligent riding of the motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-05-JX-9971 .

The evidence of PW1 remained unchallenged as the first respondent has not filed written statement and not cross-examined PW1.
9.

FIR and the complaint as per Exhibits P.1 and P.2 discloses that on the basis of complaint lodged by the first petitioner, a criminal case was registered against the rider of the motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-05-JX-9971.
Accident occurred on 02.05.2019, but the complaint was lodged on 04.05.2019.
The complainant in his complaint has given reason for delay in lodging the complaint.

According to him, immediately after the accident his father was shifted to Arunodaya hospital ,
Bengaluru , then to Prakriya hospital and later his father was shifted to Sapthagiri hospital and as the rider of the motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-05-JX-9971 had promised to provide treatment expenses , he has not lodged the complaint, but thereafter as the rider of the said motorcycle has refused to meet the treatment expenses, he has lodged the complaint.
This reason assigned by the complainant has to be accepted as a genuine reason.
Merely because there was delay of two days in lodging the complaint, the claim of the petitioners cannot be doubted.
10. The sketch and the spot mahazar as per Exhibits P.3 and P.4 reveals the state of affairs at the accident spot.
As per Exhibits P.3 and P.4, the place of accident is a junction of Defence Colony main road and 4th cross.

In Ex.P.3, it is shown that Honda Activa motorcycle bearing Reg. No.
KA-04-HS-8642 was moving on Defence Main road towards Hesaraghatta main road, at that time Veeresh.V vs Karthik.M on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166110003/

3 in the junction, the rider of the motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-05-JX-9971 has entered the main road from 4th cross road and has hit the Honda Activa motorcycle wherein the deceased was a pillion rider and complainant was a rider.

If the rider of the motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-05-JX-9971 intends to enter the main road from the cross road, then he would have taken care and caution by observing the vehicles moving on the main road.

But in the present case, the rider of the motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-05-JX-9971 has not taken care and caution, but he suddenly entered the main road without seeing the movement of the Honda Activa motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-04-HS-8642 wherein the deceased was a pillion rider.
Thus Exhibits P.3 and P.4 supports the case of the petitioner.
11. IMV report -Ex.P.5 discloses that no damages are found to Honda Activa motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-04- HS-8642 , but the right side body of the motorcycle in question was damaged.

Even by considering this damage caused to the motorcycle in question, it can be said that the rider of the motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-05- JX-9971 has hit the Honda Activa motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-04-HS-8642 from right side and as such right side body of the motorcycle in question was damaged.

Hence, by considering Exhibits P.3 to P.5, it can be safely held that the deceased met with an accident due to the rash and negligent act on the part of the rider of the motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-05-JX-9971 .
12. Exhibits P.6 and P.7 which are the P.M.Report and Inquest panchanama discloses that the death of the deceased was due to multiple injuries sustained in the accident.
Ex.P.8 is the property list wherein the motorcycle in question was seized by the police.
Exhibits P.10 and P.11 are the notice issued to the owner i.e., the first respondent by the police under Section 133 of MV Act and the reply given by first respondent to the said notice.

In Ex.P.11, the first respondent has given the details of the rider of the motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-05-JX- 9971 i.e., details of the second respondent by stating that he was the owner of the motorcycle as on the date of accident and the second respondent was the rider of the said motorcycle.
13. M.L.C. register extracts at Exs.P.26 and P.29 disclose that the deceased was admitted to Victoria hospital and Sapthagiri hospital for the treatment of injuries.

PW1 has produced case sheets at Exhibits P.27 and P.30 which disclose that the petitioner has taken treatment in Victoria hospital and Sapthagiri hospital, but inspite of the treatment, deceased succumbed to the injuries.

14. Ex.P.9 is the chargesheet filed by the police against the rider of the motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-05-JX-9971 after detailed investigation, but the same has not been challenged by the respondent No.2.

This conduct of the second respondent in not challenging the chargesheet filed against him enables the Court to draw an adverse inference against him that as the accident took place due to his negligence, he has remained silent.
All the above documents produced by PW1 remained unchallenged as the respondents have not contested the petition by filing the written statement.
Therefore, there is no reason to disbelieve the case of the petitioners.

As such by considering all these aspects, I am of the opinion that the petitioners by producing the documentary evidence and leading oral evidence of PW1 have proved that the deceased met with an accident due to the rash and negligent act on the part of the rider of the motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-05-JX-9971.
Hence, I answer point No. 1 in the affirmative.

15. Point No.2:
The petitioners claim that they are the sons of deceased Mahalingappa.
In order to prove their relationship, the petitioners have produced their Aadhar cards and also Aadhar card of the deceased as per Exhibits P.22 to P.24.
These documents disclose that the petitioners are the legal heirs of the deceased Mahalingappa and they are entitled to claim compensation for the death of their father.
Petitioners No.1 and 2 are major sons of deceased.

Merely because the petitioners No1 and 2 are majors, they cannot be denied the right to claim compensation on account of death of their father in view of the ratio laid down in Civil Appeal Nos.242-243/2020 of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India (National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Birender and others).

entities.text: Supreme Court of India (National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Birender and others)
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
In this judgment,
Pranay Sethi's case and Sarala Verma's case are referred to calculate the loss of dependency.
In the said judgment, it is observed that the major sons and daughters are also entitled to claim compensation on account of death of their father and they are also dependants on the deceased.
By applying the said ratio, it can be safely held that the petitioners No.1 and 2 , who are major children of the deceased are entitled to claim compensation on account of the death of their father.

16. PW-1 has deposed that prior to the accident, the deceased was working as a carpenter at Private concern , Bengaluru and he was getting income of Rs.25,000/p.m. and his father was maintaining the entire family.
Except the oral assertion of PW-1, absolutely, there is no proof as to avocation and income of the deceased.

In the absence of any materials before the Court, the income of the deceased which is fixed under the Minimum Wages Act has to be considered in view of the judgment of the Division Bench of our own High Court in MFA No.7404/2014 (Smt.Mariyamma and others Vs Sri Suyambulingam and another), dated 06.12.2022.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This accident has occurred in the year 2019.

As per the Minimum Wages Act, the income of the deceased has to be taken at Rs.12,000/p.m.
17.
As per the petitioners, the deceased was aged about 60 years at the time of accident.
In Aadhar card of the deceased at Ex.P.23, his date of birth is mentioned as 04.07.1950.
By considering this date of birth , it can be said that the deceased was aged about 69 years.

Depending upon the said age, as per the decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 (Sarala Verma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation),
the multiplier applicable to the present case is 5.
18.

entities.text: 2009 ACJ 1298 (Sarala Verma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As the deceased is aged more than 60 years, the question of considering the future prospects do not arise.
Income of the deceased is taken at Rs.12,000/p.m.

As the deceased died leaving behind the petitioners Nos.1 and 2 , as per Sarla Verma's Case reported in 2009 ACJ 1298, 1/3rd of the income of the deceased requires to be deducted towards the personal expenses of the deceased.
1/3rd of Rs.12,000/- would be Rs.4,000/-.
After deducting the same from Rs.12,000/-, the balance comes to Rs.8,000/-.
The annual income of the deceased works out to Rs.96,000/-.
As I have already discussed above, the multiplier applicable to the present case is 5.
If we multiply the annual income of the deceased by the multiplier, the same works out to Rs.4,80,000/- .
Hence, the petitioners are entitled to Rs.4,80,000/- towards loss of income and this amount would be awarded to the petitioners under the head Loss of Dependency.
19. As discussed above, the petitioners are the dependants on the income of the deceased, who died in the accident.

Hence, it can be safely held that the petitioners are also entitled for loss of estate,
funeral and obsequies expenses .

As per the ratio laid down in Praney Sethi's case under the conventional heads, the petitioners are awarded Rs.15,000/- towards loss of estate and Rs.15,000/-
Veeresh.V vs Karthik.M on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166110003/
5 towards funeral expenses.
20.

As per the ratio laid down in the decision reported in (2018)18 SCC 130 ( Magma General Insurance Co.Ltd., Vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram and Others), the petitioners No.1 and 2 are entitled for loss of parental consortium at Rs.40,000/- each which is amounting to Rs.80,000/-.

sentences.text: 21. Medical Expenses: PW-1 has deposed that immediately after the accident his father was shifted to Arunodaya hospital, Bengaluru, wherein first aid treatment was given and thereafter his father was shifted to Prakriya hospital and then to Sapthagiri hospital for treatment.

The petitioners have summoned PWs 2 and 3 who are the technician and clerk in the medical records department at Victoria hospital and Sapthagiri hospital and they have produced case sheets as per Exs.P.27 and P.30 and X-rays as per Ex.P.31.

PW-1 has also produced OPD case sheet , outpatient slip, lab records, ultrasonography reports, biochemistry reports, serology reports, haematology reports,
x-ray films as per Exs.P.12 to P.18 and P.21.

All these medical records disclose that the deceased was shifted to Sapthagiri hospital and Victoria hospital for the treatment of the accidental injuries, but inspite of the treatment given, the deceased succumbed to the injuries on 16.05.2019.

These medical records disclose that the deceased was inpatient in Sapthagiri hospital from 03.05.2019 to 16.05.2019 and he was inpatient in Victoria hospital on 16.05.2019 and he succumbed to the accidental injuries on the same day.
22. PW1 has deposed that he has spent Rs.1,00,000/- towards medical expenses for the treatment of his father.
In support of his evidence, he has produced medical bills and prescriptions as per Exs.P.19 and P.20.
Ex.P.19 are amounting to Rs.66,539/-.

From the medical records placed before the Court, it can be said that major treatment was given to the deceased for the accidental injuries in Sapthagiri hospital and only for one day the deceased was treated in Victoria hospital .
) is the inpatient bill of Sapthagiri hospital amounting to Rs.43,120/-.
PW1 has produced advance receipts for having paid the said amount in advance .
Hence, it can be said that the petitioners have spent the said amount towards treatment of the deceased in Sapthagiri hospital and they are entitled for the said amount.
Majority of the bills are pharmacy bills.
But they do not contain the seal of the shop.
Some of the bills are not supported by prescriptions.
Some of the bills are of Prakriya hospital and its pharmacy.

However, by considering the nature of the injuries and the type of treatment undergone by the deceased, it can be said that the petitioners have spent some amount towards medicines, conveyance, nourishment and attendant charges during the lifetime of the deceased.
As such, the petitioners are entitled for Rs.85,000/- towards medical expenses.

23. In view of the above said reasons, I am inclined to award compensation to the petitioners under the following heads:

Annual income of the 8,000x12  petitioner 96,000 iv Compensation after 96,000x5 4,80,000-00  multiplier applied v Loss of estate 15,000-00 vi Funeral expenses 15,000-00 vii Parental consortium to 40,000/-each 80,000-00 Viii Medical expenses 85,000-00
Thus, the petitioners are awarded compensation of Rs.6,75,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of the petition till realisation.
24. So far as the liability is concerned, according to the petitioners, the first respondent is the owner and second respondent is the rider of the motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-05-JX-9971.
Though the first respondent has appeared through his counsel, but he has not contested the petition by filing written statement.
In the reply notice at Ex.P.11, the first respondent has stated that there was no insurance to the motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-05-JX-9971 as on the date of accident.
The second respondent being the rider of the motorcycle has remained exparte.

As there was no insurance policy to the motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-05-JX-9971 as on the date of accident , I am of the opinion that the respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount of Rs.6,75,000/- to the petitioners with interest at 6%p.a. from the date of petition till realization.
Accordingly, I answer point No.2 partly in the affirmative.
25. Point No.3 :

In view of my findings on point Nos.1 and 2 and for the reasons stated therein, I proceed to pass the following: -
ORDER

The claim petition filed by the petitioners is allowed in part with costs against the respondents No.1 and 2 awarding compensation of Rs.6,75,000/-
(Rupees Six lakhs Seventy Five Thousand only) with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the date of deposit in Court.

The respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount with interest to the petitioners and they are directed to deposit the compensation amount in Court within 3 months from the date of this order.
The compensation amount is apportioned amongst the petitioners No.1 and 2 equally.

After deposit of the compensation amount, 50% each share of the petitioners No.1 and 2 with proportionate interest shall be deposited in their respective names in any of the nationalized or scheduled bank of their choice for a period of 3 years.
Remaining 50% each with proportionate interest is ordered to be released to the petitioners No.1 and 2.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/- .
Draw an Award accordingly.
